label: Огромный / Крошечный
description: Огромный vs крошечный: huge/tiny contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Огромный' takes the masculine ending to match 'дом'. The sentence frames the size in a natural possessive context.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Крошечная' takes the feminine ending to match 'комната'. The form is anchored in a concrete household observation.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Огромное' takes the neuter ending to match 'окно'. The sentence shows the learner switching endings inside a real room description.
Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Крошечный' takes the masculine ending to match 'ключ'. The form sits in a simple spatial scene.

missions.phrase: Здесь огромный город и крошечная деревня.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Contrast across two genders. 'Огромный' matches masculine 'город' while 'крошечная' matches feminine 'деревня'. The sentence pairs both endings in one vivid image.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Огромные' takes the plural ending to match 'руки'. The sentence shows the same adjective applied to a plural body-part noun.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Крошечные' takes the plural ending to match 'пуговицы'. The sentence reinforces the plural form in a tidy everyday scene.
Strategic focus: Feminine short form. 'Огромна' is the predicative short form agreeing with 'квартира'. The sentence shows how the short form states a judged quality rather than naming an object.

missions.phrase: Этот двор больше, чем тот крошечный сад.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Comparative versus full adjective. 'Больше' is the comparative form set against the full adjective 'крошечный', which agrees with masculine 'сад'. The sentence contrasts a comparative with a plain attributive use.

missions.phrase: У слона огромные уши, а у мыши крошечные.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Direct plural contrast. 'Огромные' and 'крошечные' both take the plural ending to match 'уши', with the second clause eliding the noun. The sentence pairs the two adjectives in a memorable size comparison.
